pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 8.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: ADVERTISEMENTS AND NEWS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are advertisements important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe objects from adverts and news for information
2. enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 8.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: ADVERTISEMENTS AND NEWS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 8.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: ADVERTISEMENTS AND NEWS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe objects from adverts and news for information

What this means
In this part you learn to describe objects from adverts and news for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe objects from adverts and news for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe objects from adverts and news for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading

What this means
In this part you learn to enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe objects from adverts and news for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News to a partner. (skill: enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe objects from adverts and news for information.
3. Practise this skill: enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are advertisements important?
2. How do we describe objects?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Advertisements and News means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe objects from adverts and news for information.
5. Be able to: enjoy advertisements and news items for extensive reading.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
